title: High and Low
prompt: Photograph one ordinary thing twice: once from as low as you can safely get, and once from as high as you can safely reach.
questions: Which version makes it look bigger, or more important?
What came into the frame when you moved?
Which one looks least like the way we normally see it?
Would getting even lower help, or has it stopped improving?
technical_reminder: For the high version, hold the camera above your head and tilt it down; for the low one, rest it on the ground. Take the photograph, then look at the screen — do not try to squint through the viewfinder.
safety_note: Crouch or kneel rather than lying down, and check the ground and the traffic before getting low.

variation.text: Make an ordinary object look enormous, then make the same object look tiny.

review_prompt: Which viewpoint makes the ordinary thing most surprising?
